bullets: Do You Have Any Farting Unicorns? is the super silly card game that makes Go Fish outrageously fun. Ask your opponents for Farting Unicorns, Giant Underwear, Ants in Your Pants, and 10 more hilariously illustrated card types. Try not to burst out laughing when it's your turn to say them out loud. A fresh, funny twist on the classic card game the whole family already knows and loves.

HOW TO PLAY: Shuffle and deal 5–7 cards each depending on player count. On your turn, ask any opponent for a card type you already hold, just like Go Fish, except your requests sound like "Dad, do you have any Books about Poop?" If they have the card, they give you ALL their matching cards and you get another turn. If not, they say "Go fish!" and you draw from the pile. Collect all 4 matching cards to complete a Set. When the draw pile runs out, the player with the most Sets wins!

PERFECT FOR FAMILIES, CLASSROOMS & PARTIES: Whether it's family game night, a birthday party, a holiday gathering or a classroom party, Do You Have Any Farting Unicorns? gets everyone laughing from the very first card. A screen-free, giggles-guaranteed favorite for grandparent visits, road trips, camping trips, and family reunions. Makes a great gift for kids ages 4–12 and anyone who's young at heart.

WHAT'S IN THE BOX: 52 beautifully illustrated prompt cards featuring 13 hilariously silly categories × 4 cards each, plus 1 rules card. Card types include: Farting Unicorns, Horns On Your Head, Talking Toilets, T-Rex Teachers, Ants in Your Pants and so much more! Friends (and giant underwear) not included.

For 2–6 players ages 4 and up. Rounds last just 5–15 minutes, fast enough to play again and again (and you will). Easy enough for early readers and non-readers alike, thanks to bold, expressive illustrations on every single card.

reviews.name: Rebecca
reviews.title: Good game for 3-5 year olds
reviews.body: I bought this for my 6 year old who recently completed kindergarten as a fun way to practice math over the summer. She enjoys it (especially the challenges) and it’s well made (hence the four stars), but I think it’s just a little too easy for her age group.
